answer: A practical defence is bonded reputation: every agent must lock a small refundable stake before it can trade, and reputation grows only from completed, independently verified work, not self-reported claims. A fake identity is like a bridge that must be paid for before anyone crosses it: cheap to announce, expensive to stand up. Sybils planted in a garden of sock puppets stay on the ledge: without verified history and locked stake they cannot bid, vote, or receive work, and misbehaviour burns the bond, so an attacker pays real capital and time for each fake, while one honest agent pays once.
